questions.skill: Precise definition of perpendicular lines
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Ben writes: "Perpendicular lines are lines that make a T." Explain what is imprecise, and write a precise definition.
questions.prompt_markup:
Ben writes: "Perpendicular lines are lines that make a T."
Explain what is imprecise, and write a precise definition.
questions.correct_answer: "Make a T" is not defined (a T can be tilted or have unequal angles, and lines do not stop). Precise: two lines are perpendicular if they intersect and form a right angle.
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent answer. Essential: names the vague term and gives a definition with both parts (intersect; right angle). Accept "intersect to form congruent adjacent angles".

questions.prompt: Line m passes through (0, 0) and (2, 1). Line n passes through (0, 0) and (-1, 2). Use the definition (intersect and form a right angle) to decide whether m and n are perpendicular. Show how you know the angle at (0, 0) is a right angle.
questions.prompt_markup: Line m passes through (0, 0) and (2, 1). Line n passes through (0, 0) and (-1, 2). Use the definition (intersect and form a right angle) to decide whether m and n are perpendicular. Show how you know the angle at (0, 0) is a right angle.
questions.correct_answer: Yes. They meet at (0, 0). With A(2, 1) and B(-1, 2): OA² = 5, OB² = 5, AB² = 9 + 1 = 10 = OA² + OB², so by the converse of the Pythagorean Theorem the angle at O is a right angle.
questions.grading_note: Any valid method that shows a right angle at the intersection (Pythagorean converse, or slopes ½ and -2 with a reason). Essential: the intersection and the right angle.

questions.skill: Prove consequences of the definition of perpendicular lines
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: Lines ℓ and m are perpendicular and meet at point P. Prove that all four angles at P are right angles.
questions.prompt_markup: Lines ℓ and m are perpendicular and meet at point P. Prove that all four angles at P are right angles.
questions.required_method: Start from the definition (one angle at P is a right angle). Use the linear pair (supplementary) to get the adjacent angles and vertical angles (or another linear pair) to get the fourth, with a reason for each step.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof. Essential: (1) definition gives one 90° angle; (2) each adjacent angle forms a linear pair with it, so it is 180° - 90° = 90°; (3) the fourth angle is vertical to the first (or forms a linear pair with a 90° angle). Invalid: "they look like right angles".

questions.required_method: Linear pair angles add to 180°; congruent means equal measures, so each is 90°; then apply the definition.

questions.skill: Reason about perpendicular lines with a third line, in a plane and in space
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: In a plane, lines a and b are both perpendicular to line t. Prove that a and b are parallel.
questions.prompt_markup: In a plane, lines a and b are both perpendicular to line t. Prove that a and b are parallel.
questions.required_method: Use the corresponding angles that a and b make with t (both right angles, so congruent) and the converse of the corresponding angles postulate; or argue by contradiction with the triangle angle sum.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof. Essential: both corresponding angles at t are 90°, so they are congruent; congruent corresponding angles make the lines parallel. Alternative: if a and b met, they would form a triangle with t having two 90° angles, so its angle sum would exceed 180°. Invalid: "they look parallel".
